title: Profound vs. Peec AI: Which AEO tool supports your growth strategy?
content:
According to McKinsey, 50% of consumers now use AI-powered search, and more than 70% rely on it to ask questions and gather information. This shift in search behavior means SEO leaders must evolve. Modern workflows need to incorporate Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) strategies so brands can not only rank on page one of Google, but also gain visibility inside AI-generated answers across platforms like Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, and Perplexity.
This means marketing leaders need to know what’s going on with their brand in AI search. How are AI tools referring to it, citing it, and in relation to what search queries are brands showing up?
Enter Profound and Peec AI. These AI Visibility tools are designed to help marketing teams monitor, measure, and improve their content for search generative experiences (SGE) while tracking how AI answer engines represent their brand.
As AEO becomes a strategic priority, marketers are evaluating Profound AI vs. Peec AI for AEO and seeking a clear comparison between the two. This guide breaks down what each platform offers, how they differ, and which solution best supports a team’s strategy.
As AI-powered answer engines reshape how people discover information, marketers need new ways to measure and influence brand visibility beyond traditional search. Platforms like Peec AI and Profound AI sit at the center of this shift. Both are designed for Answer Engine Optimization (AEO), helping teams understand how their brand appears inside AI-generated responses across tools like ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity.
At a high level, they solve similar problems — tracking AI mentions, citations, and visibility — but they differ in depth, complexity, and intended use cases.
Marketers should consider tools like Peec AI or Profound AI because AI answer engines are increasingly shaping what customers see and trust, and these platforms reveal whether — and how — a brand appears in those responses. Both platforms help marketers understand and optimize how their brand shows up in AI responses, an increasingly important part of modern search visibility as AI answers replace traditional blue links.
Peec AI is an AI visibility and search analytics platform focused on helping teams quickly understand how their brand appears across AI answer engines. It tracks core AEO metrics like:
Where Peec stands out is in its simplicity and speed to insight. The platform surfaces clear, digestible data that makes it easy to benchmark performance and spot gaps without requiring heavy setup or technical integration. This makes it a strong fit for:
The tradeoff is that Peec is more focused on measurement than activation. While it helps marketers and SEO professionals understand how their brand shows up, it offers fewer built-in tools for turning those insights into execution across content and workflows.
Profound AI is an enterprise-grade AEO platform designed to measure AI visibility and help teams actively improve it. Profound’s key strength is its actionability at scale. Like Peec, it tracks mentions, citations, and presence across AI systems. But, the tool goes further with:
Profound is built for organizations that want to operationalize AEO and link AI visibility data to content strategy, SEO workflows, and business outcomes. This makes it a strong fit for:
The tradeoff is complexity. Compared to Peec, Profound may require more onboarding and ongoing management to fully realize its value.

For marketers investing in AEO, coverage matters, especially as more AI search tools enter the market. If a tool only tracks one or two AI engines, marketers are operating with partial visibility. In modern-day search, buyers move between Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Perplexity, and other answer engines, so a team’s monitoring platform must reflect that search experience.
Peec AI supports Google AI Overviews and other major answer engines, but on the Starter, Advanced, and Pro plans, teams can choose only three engines to track, or pay extra to add others. At the Enterprise level, teams can track an unlimited number of models, including Grok, Claude, and GPT 5 Search.
Its coverage is designed to monitor core generative platforms that influence buyer research, helping marketers track mentions, citations, and competitive presence across multiple engines without overly complex configuration.
Profound uses front-end capture for AI answer tracking. The Starter plan only includes ChatGPT, however. To access tracking for the other models, teams will have to upgrade to either the Growth plan (ChatGPT, Perplexity, and AI Overviews) or the Enterprise plan (those three models plus Gemini, Copilot, Meta AI, Grok, DeepSeat, Claude, and AI Mode).
For marketing and SEO leaders, tracking AI visibility is only valuable if the data leads to action. Reporting depth determines whether a team can simply see mentions or truly understand positioning, competitive gaps, and opportunities to influence AI-generated narratives.
Peec AI goes beyond visibility reporting with a built-in “Act on Insights” feature that translates AEO data into specific next steps for marketers. Rather than simply showing whether a brand appears in AI-generated answers, Peec surfaces actionable recommendations, like building a presence on cited review platforms or joining relevant community discussions. This helps teams prioritize authority-building opportunities based on what’s actually driving AI citations.
Profound leans into deeper analysis and contextual tracking. Profound uses front-end capture for AI answer tracking, which allows teams to monitor how responses appear in live environments and evaluate how answers are structured, cited, and positioned.
This approach can provide more granular insight into competitive dynamics, such as which brands are cited first and how prompts influence outcomes. For teams running advanced AEO programs, this level of detail supports more deliberate optimization and content strategy decisions.
AEO can’t live in a silo to drive measurable growth. Marketing leaders need AI visibility data that connects to their CRM, content workflows, and revenue analytics. Without integration, AEO becomes another disconnected metric, and measuring its impact is inefficient.
Peec AI offers flexible data export and integration options. It currently offers a Looker Studio integration to export and visualize visibility data in customizable dashboards. This enables teams to centralize core AEO metrics alongside SEO and other performance data in a familiar reporting environment. A data API and CSV exports are also available for teams that need to pull visibility data into existing workflows.
For marketers focused on basic dashboards and visibility reporting, the Looker Studio integration makes it easy to start visualizing AEO trends alongside other metrics. However, outside of Looker Studio and API access, Peec’s integration footprint remains limited. If a team’s workflow requires deeper connectivity into enterprise systems — such as CRM, content hubs, or analytics platforms — Peec’s current integrations may feel lightweight.
Profound offers a broad ecosystem of integrations designed to embed AEO insights into content and marketing workflows. Beyond dashboard exports, Profound Agents connect natively to content management systems (WordPress, Sanity, Contentful, and Webflow), productivity and collaboration tools (Slack, Gamma), and Google Search Console. Teams can act on AEO data without leaving the platforms they already use.
This allows teams to bring AI visibility signals into:
Profound clearly leads in integrations and workflow connectivity.
The cost of AI can be an immediate and non-negotiable barrier to choosing between Profound vs. Peec AI for GEO. Profound may immediately outprice some businesses because it is expensive, especially if there are plans to scale to the large packages.
Peec AI is known for competitive pricing and fast onboarding, making it attractive for startups, mid-market teams, and agencies that want rapid deployment. Low barriers to entry allow marketing teams to begin tracking AI visibility quickly. Peec offers a robust knowledge base with videos for every task marketers would need to complete to get set up.
Peec is particularly appealing for organizations that want to experiment with AEO and scale gradually. Agencies managing multiple clients may also appreciate a lighter-weight onboarding process that enables quicker rollout across accounts.
Teams can try Peec free for seven days, then it’s paid packages, starting from:
Profound is positioned more strongly toward enterprise organizations. Profound provides enterprise-grade security and compliance features, which can be essential for large brands operating in regulated industries or global markets.
Profound’s pricing and onboarding model typically align with enterprise procurement processes, including structured implementation, stakeholder alignment, and governance considerations. While this may involve a longer ramp-up period, it supports larger organizations that require data controls, auditability, and scalable deployment across global teams.
With Profound, teams jump straight into paid packages. From my experience, there’s no free trial, but CTAs do suggest you can try it for free. Paid packages start from:
Note: Profound’s starter package includes only ChatGPT.
The right choice of Profound vs. Peec AI for AEO depends less on features in isolation and more on team structure, growth stage, and operational maturity. AEO tools don’t create growth on their own. They amplify the systems already in place. Here’s how to think about it by scenario.
HubSpot recently launched HubSpot AEO , its answer to in-depth AEO analysis and ongoing AI visibility strategy. This GEO tool includes:
With HubSpot AEO, marketing teams can track how their brand performs across answer engines over time, with visibility scores updated continuously as AI platforms evolve.
HubSpot AEO is available as a standalone tool for $50 per month or inside Marketing Hub Pro and Enterprise. Recommendations connect directly to HubSpot’s content and social tools, so teams can act on AEO insights without leaving the platform if they already use HubSpot.
Profound prioritizes comprehensive analytics, broad engine coverage, and enterprise integration. It’s well-suited for teams that want deep insight into how AI answer engines interpret and display content. Peec AI focuses on straightforward visibility tracking and actionable recommendations, enabling teams to quickly identify where their brand appears and what strategic actions to take next.
Peec AI supports seven different platforms, though teams can only choose three to monitor unless they add on additional engines. Teams that use Peec AI Enterprise can monitor unlimited engines, including ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, Google AI Mode, AI Overviews, Gemini, Copilot, and Grok.
Profound offers broad coverage across platforms, though it’s starter plan only includes ChatGPT coverage. Upgrading will give teams access to major and emerging engines such as Perplexity, Claude, Google AI Mode, Gemini, Copilot, Grok, and more.
Profound is generally stronger in enterprise-grade readiness, with features designed for security, governance, and large-scale deployments. Organizations operating in regulated industries or with strict data policies tend to prefer its compliance and integration capabilities. Peec AI remains valuable for teams that prioritize quick adoption and clear insights, but may require additional controls or manual processes for enterprise governance needs.
Peec AI’s pricing and ease of onboarding make it attractive for agencies that need to roll out AEO tracking across a portfolio of clients quickly. Its actionable reporting and visibility dashboards help agencies demonstrate impact without steep learning curves. Profound can also serve agencies, especially those supporting enterprise clients or complex global strategies, but its depth and governance features may align better with larger, more structured agency engagements.
Teams benefit most from Peec AI or Profound AI at different stages of their AEO maturity and operational complexity. Peec AI is ideal when the goal is to quickly understand AI visibility, benchmark competitors, and generate clear, actionable insights without heavy implementation — making it a strong fit for teams early in their AEO journey or those prioritizing speed and simplicity.
Profound AI, on the other hand, delivers the most value when AEO is becoming a core growth lever, requiring deeper analytics and integration into content, CRM, and reporting workflows. For organizations looking to operationalize AEO at scale and tie AI visibility directly to business outcomes, Profound provides the infrastructure to move from insight to sustained execution.
Before committing to any platform, teams should benchmark where they stand today. HubSpot’s AEO Grader lets you analyze your brand’s AI visibility for free — no credit card required. It provides visibility snapshots, competitive insights, sentiment analysis, and practical recommendations so you can understand how AI answer engines currently represent your brand. Whether you choose Profound, Peec AI, or another solution, starting with objective performance data gives you clarity.
